title: Tomas Haake - Wikipedia
notes: Tomas Nils Haake, born 13 July 1971, Örnsköldsvik, Sweden; Meshuggah's drummer and main lyricist; 'known for his polymeters and technical ability'; Sonor SQ2, dual 22x18 bass drums, Sabian; influences Phil Rudd, Bill Ward, Lars Ulrich, Dave Weckl, Neil Peart, Terry Bozzio; Modern Drummer readers' poll, Metal, July 2008; Rolling Stone's 100 greatest drummers, 93rd.

title: Meshuggah - Wikipedia
notes: Haake joined in 1990. 'On Rational Gaze (from Nothing), Haake plays simple 4/4 time, hitting the snare on each third beat, for 16 bars' (citing Begrand, PopMatters); Hagström: 'Everything we do is based around a 4/4 core' (Decibel, 2005). Catch Thirtythree is 'the only Meshuggah album on which programmed drums have been used'; Haake returned to the kit on obZen; The Violent Sleep of Reason was recorded live in the studio. Discography with years.

title: Nothing (Meshuggah album) - Wikipedia
notes: The 2006 reissue: 'The drums were also re-recorded by using the original drum hits as triggers for new audio produced with virtual drum software.' The hits are his.

title: obZen - Wikipedia
notes: 'Tomas Haake made his return as a studio drummer for the record after the Drumkit From Hell drum software was used on Catch Thirtythree'; Drumkit from Hell 'was an auxiliary sound source', not programmed. Track list: Combustion, Electric Red, Bleed, Lethargica, obZen, This Spiteful Snake, Pineal Gland Optics, Pravus, Dancers to a Discordant System.

title: Web Exclusive Interview With Meshuggah's Tomas Haake (Modern Drummer, Dave Previ, 17 June 2013)
notes: 'Sometimes it's the feet doing the riff, and the hands are going straight over it.' 'Whoever writes the song also writes the drum parts. Usually not a lot is changed in those drum parts except for the fills.' 'I don't have a ride cymbal. It's just big crashes and Chinas.' 'I can't go for 16th notes at super-fast tempos for a long period of time.'

title: Tomas Haake: Meshuggah's Djentle Giant (DRUM! Magazine, Andrew Lentz, 10 September 2012)
notes: 'I only do the hits with the guitar hits. So the toms are doing what the guitars are doing together with the bass drum instead of being a fill that's on top of something else.' 'For us it's usually like at 16/32 or 8/32 bars is when [the cycle] kind of starts over'; the odd cycles are not odd time signatures 'because it's all built around 4/4.' 'I'm not counting while playing.' The hi-hat 'has to be going. That's my solid point.' Rimshots, even on the toms. Comfort at about 140; 'past 160–170 it's getting awkward.' Kit: Sonor SQ2, 22x18 bass drum, bronze snare, 14in tom, 15in and 18in floor toms, Sabian crashes and Chinese cymbals, a 22in ride played as a crash; Trick pedals.

title: Tomas Haake: Meshuggah Goes It Alone (DRUM! Magazine, David Weiss, 20 May 2010)
notes: 'This whole album [obZen] is straight 4/4 all through'; 'a pattern of snare and kick could be nine hits over an 8/8 bar', 'alternative cycles or odd groupings' rather than odd time signatures. Fills 'totally, intimately connected with the riff'; Electric Red's 'patiently rolling, relatively spare tom and kick arrangement'. Bleed: 'the most intricate drum part work I've ever done'; most parts are written by whoever writes the song.

title: Meshuggah's Tomas Haake: 5 Reasons He's A Drumming Genius (Drumeo Beat, Aaron Edgar, updated 6 July 2023)
notes: Bleed: a herta on the feet (RLR L RLR L) against a straightforward 4/4 beat on the hands; the herta moves over the bar line; he played it lighter, 'tap dance', to last the song. 'For a few months, we didn't know if we were gonna have it on the album or not.'

title: Inside the mind of Tomas Haake, Meshuggah's modern musical genius (Metal Hammer via Louder, Dom Lawson, 5 November 2016)
notes: 'I wasn't a natural, not at all. It took quite some time to be any good at it.' With Mårten Hagström from 13 or 14; 'We loved Metallica ... We did try to do some odd time signatures, so I guess that led into Meshuggah in some way.'

title: Ligature Marks - Complete Polymeter Breakdown and Drum Transcription (Drumstickler, AJ, 27 September 2022)
notes: The kick carries a phrase 37 eighth notes long while the snare hits the three of almost every bar; the verse alternates phrases of 21 and 20 eighths; the outro a 22-quarter polymeter; the cycle completes in 16 bars, with fills between repetitions.
